firmware_alternative.name: ACPI MADT Multiprocessor Wakeup
firmware_alternative.selection_condition: A valid MADT type 0x10 entry is one path that installs acpi_wakeup_cpu as wakeup_secondary_cpu_64 callback. Other APIC/platform code can also install wakeup_secondary_cpu_64 or wakeup_secondary_cpu callbacks.
firmware_alternative.entry_mode: The ACPI 6.6 Intel mailbox WakeupVector contract enters with long mode and paging enabled, identity mapped page, and IF=0.

selected_project_path.name: INIT/SIPI
basis: The current project board MADT has one enabled Processor Local APIC entry for UID/APIC ID 0 and has no Multiprocessor Wakeup entry; no alternate wakeup callback is part of the current board contract.
The Stage 6 first vertical slice explicitly requires BSP INIT/SIPI and an AP real-mode trampoline.

smpboot.c dispatches in order: wakeup_secondary_cpu_64 callback, wakeup_secondary_cpu callback, then wakeup_secondary_cpu_via_init fallback. A board MADT without type 0x10 does not rule out another callback override. The selected callback for the final VM CPU/APIC configuration is pending runtime/source-path verification.
selected_project_path.apic_mode_limit: The project board candidate records BSP xAPIC as selected-but-unverified (S4-00c). Linux configuration alone does not establish guest xAPIC/x2APIC runtime selection.
selected_project_path.avoid_publishing_madt_type_0x10: Publishing the entry would install the firmware mailbox callback, a different AP handoff contract that the current VM board does not implement; other overrides must also be checked.

init_sipi_sequence.destination: phys_apicid target argument; with the project xAPIC candidate this is physical destination mode, but guest runtime mode remains unverified.
init_sipi_sequence.init_assert: ICR = LEVEL_TRIGGER | ASSERT | DELIVERY_INIT; wait for ICR idle.

init_delay.default_modern_cpu: 0 microseconds for Intel family/model >= Pentium Pro, AMD family >= 0x0f, or Hygon family >= 0x18.

delay_provider.mechanism: The source calls udelay(); arch/x86/lib/delay.c converts this using loops_per_jiffy and the configured delay_fn. The kernel can select TSC-based delay (use_tsc_delay) or other delay providers.
delay_provider.runtime_provider: Pending: S4-35 pins no guest CPU feature set/boot log showing which provider the final VM uses.

init_sipi_sequence.init_deassert: ICR = LEVEL_TRIGGER | DELIVERY_INIT with ASSERT clear; wait for ICR idle.

sipi.count: Two attempts when the boot APIC is integrated; zero if it is not integrated.
sipi.delay_when_init_delay_zero: 10 microseconds after send, wait for ICR idle, then 10 microseconds before reading ESR.
sipi.delay_when_init_delay_nonzero: 300 microseconds after send, wait for ICR idle, then 200 microseconds before reading ESR.
sipi.retry: The loop stops on send or APIC delivery error; otherwise it may issue the second SIPI.

init_sipi_sequence.caveat: Actual default delay depends on the guest CPU vendor/family/model and kernel command line, neither of which is pinned by S4-35.

trampoline_image_evidence.extraction: Read the ELF64 section table and symbol table; extracted symbol bytes from .init.data to /private/tmp/s6-02-real_mode_blob.bin. Extraction was read-only against the staged artifact.
path_for_project_INIT_SIPI: SIPI vector enters pa_trampoline_start at offset 0x1000 in real mode.
The real-mode path loads descriptor tables, verifies long-mode capability and enters protected-mode startup_32 at offset 0x2000.
startup_32 enables PAE, loads CR3, configures EFER.LME and CR0 paging, then far-jumps to long-mode startup_64 at offset 0x20f0.
startup_64 jumps indirectly through tr_start at offset 0x5000 to the kernel's common secondary startup path.

disassembly_tools.confirmed: The actual image's 32-bit startup_32 range and 64-bit startup_64 entry were decoded from vmlinux-debug using --arch-name=x86 and --arch-name=x86-64.
disassembly_tools.pending: The available tool has no x86 16-bit decode mode. Run the full real-mode instruction and byte inventory using the prescribed x86 bench toolchain before S6-02 acceptance.

trampoline_image_evidence.extraction_command_basis: ELF .init.data file offset 0x31d2000 + (real_mode_blob VMA 0xffffffff83ff6000 - section VMA 0xffffffff83fd2000) = 0x31f6000; symbol size 0x6264. dd output was byte-compared with the ELF64 parser extraction.

board_firmware.current_madt: One enabled Processor Local APIC record: Processor UID 0, APIC ID 0. No MADT type 0x10 Multiprocessor Wakeup record.
board_firmware.smp_requirement: For an n-vCPU APIC board, ACPI 6.6 requires one enabled Local APIC record per vCPU, stable APIC IDs, and matching processor Device objects in the ACPI namespace under \_SB with _HID=ACPI0007 and matching _UID. The project currently emits its namespace in DSDT; ACPI does not require that a Device be in DSDT rather than SSDT.

windows.INIT_SIPI_real_mode_trampoline: No Microsoft source found that establishes this as the generic Windows x64 AP startup path; retain the planned stage 8 trace check.

processor_objects.ACPI_6_6: For the APIC interrupt model, each processor has a Processor Local APIC MADT entry and corresponding processor Device in the ACPI namespace; ACPI 6.6 §8.4 specifies Device under \_SB with _HID ACPI0007 and _UID matching MADT. DSDT versus SSDT is not prescribed.
processor_objects.Microsoft_scope: The Microsoft processor-identification page found here is scoped to SoC-based platforms; it does not establish a generic client Windows x64 requirement or absence behavior.
processor_objects.result: Keep generic Windows-specific absence behavior open for stage 8 trace; emit conforming ACPI 6.6 processor namespace objects in the project's current DSDT.
